backlog.title: Local input recovery — NEW unshipped PRD requirement: durable editor-input capture, restore, retirement, blank-answer rejection
backlog.description: spec/state-and-persistence.md §Local input recovery (added at spec ec61eb1) is explicitly 'New requirements, not shipped': the shipped panel keeps drafts in extension memory only (src/draft-store.ts has no durable layer; nothing writes drafts to disk). Scope per the updated PRD: capture-on-edit durable saves for EVERY editor duty (Other/write-in, text answer, elaboration, batch note, side-chat composer), atomic recovery points that survive hard kills mid-typing, retirement on deliberate discard/user replacement/successful handoff, restore + seeding rules (newer matching draft > exact recorded answer.value > blank; never seed Other with an option value; intentional deletion-to-empty is an edit), and blank-answer rejection at the shared final mutation applyAnswer across ALL ingress (panel, side-chat apply, non-TUI answers[], submit reconciliation) — trim tests emptiness only, nonblank stores untrimmed, rejection precedes any answer/status change/advance/submission and keeps editor focus with an inline reason ('Answer cannot be blank'). FR-28 gains matching-draft restore on session start; commitment 6 now defers to this section and 'cross-restart draft persistence' is REMOVED from non-goals; the side-chat TRANSCRIPT stays ephemeral (SIDECHAT-002 unchanged — recovery covers the user's composer text, not the conversation; decisions.md 'Later decision — panel input recovery'). subtasks.title: Atomic persistence, durability, monotonicity, and honest failure
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PRD 'Recovery point' — a completed local save must survive restart within the OS and storage system's durability guarantees; replace atomically so an interrupted write leaves the previous or new complete value, never a torn one. Older writes and incidental empty buffers (initialization, view change, send cleanup) must not overwrite newer user edits. On write failure keep the last durable value AND the live edit; never claim the edit was saved. Recovery guarantees the latest completed save — not keystrokes the editor never received or a write still in flight.
2. INPUT: capture wiring from P3.M2.T1.S1; the design's atomicity/ordering strategy.
3. LOGIC: Implement temp-file+rename (or equivalent) atomic replace; enforce monotonic per-field ordering (reject/ignore out-of-order writes); classify incidental empties so they never clobber; on write failure surface nothing false (no 'saved' indication) and keep both values. Scripted tests: interrupted write -> previous-or-new complete value; older-write-after-newer-edit ignored; in-flight write not promised.
4. OUTPUT: durable store with atomicity/monotonicity/failure tests, consumed by P3.M2.T1.S3 and P3.M3.T1.*.
5. DOCS: none at this layer.

For quick clarification in side chat, the active draft/last user prompt suffices; no transcript archive is required. A refused or failed send or aborted turn leaves the prompt recoverable for manual retry without overwriting newer typing.
2. INPUT: durable store from P3.M2.T1.S2; the deliberate-exit seams (editor discard/clear, user replacement, commit/send handoff sites in actions.ts / sidechat send path).

Script acceptance cases: (2) type continuously + paste multiline Unicode with surrounding whitespace, kill during typing (simulated) -> recovery points progressed without an idle interval and the last completed one restores expanded text exactly; (3) fail a write, delay an older write past a newer edit/discard, switch branches with the same question ID -> no false saved indication, no clobber, no resurrection, no cross-branch restore; (4-send-half) refuse/fail a chat send and abort a turn -> reopen with the prompt recoverable and no duplicate send.
